• Scientific name: Hypostomus isbrueckeri Reis, Weber & Malabarba, 1990
  • Type locality: Rio Conceição, Ijui, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
  • Etymology: Greek, hypo = under + Greek, stoma = mouth. Named to honour Dr. Issaäc J.H. Isbrücker.
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2018).

Family: Loricariidae. Size: 30 cm. Temperature: 20-24°C. pH: 6.5-7.2.

The genus Hypostomus has 7 soft rays in the dorsal fin, whereas the similar-looking Pterygoplichthys species have 10 soft dorsal fin rays.
South America: Middle and upper Uruguay River basin (La Plata basin).

South America: middle and upper Uruguay River basin. Type locality: Rio Conceição, Ijui, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.

Hypostomus isbrueckeri is endemic to Brazil and is distributed in the upper and middle Uruguay River basins. The species is widely distributed, frequent and abundant. As no significant threats to its population have been identified, it is categorised as Least Concern (LC) (IUCN 2022).
As with most of this genus, it will do well in a larger aquarium, and the aquarium should be well filtered. Water parameters can be quite diverse for this genus.
Omnivore with a liking for green foods, tablet foods and frozen foods.
Mature males have white to yellow seams on the distal margins of the caudal fin.
Breeding is unreported; there is no breeding report.

Description: Head covered with dermal ossifications dorsally, except for an oval naked area on the snout tip. Dorsal margin of orbit not or very slightly elevated, continuing in a very inconspicuous ridge on the posttemporal plate. Usually three scutes border the posterior margin of the supraoccipital; these scutes are sometimes fragmented into four or five small scutelets. Body very low; dorsal profile gently descending from the origin of the dorsal fin to the end of the caudal peduncle. Caudal peduncle roughly ovate in cross-section, slightly flattened ventrally. Dorsal scutes between the end of the dorsal fin base and the adipose fin spine are flat in their dorsal portions; those closer to the dorsal fin sometimes have a central area without odontodes.

Etymology: The specific name isbrueckeri honours the noted ichthyologist Dr. Isaäc J. H. Isbrücker.
